action: Reach out directly to Kevin O'Brien to receive and review the one-page brief he has prepared. Frame it as a collegial professional conversation — not as a manager checking in, but as a peer who respects the work he has done. I want to understand what he has written and whether it relates to my position change, the branch situation, or something else. This is also an opportunity to be honest with him: I am no longer in the branch manager seat and he should know that before he hears it through other channels. Maintaining his trust is more valuable now than managing appearances.
